done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: `calendarYear` accepts a year only when the whole question is essentially the year or its immediate prefix/suffix matches a narrow whitelist. A natural same-thread follow-up such as “Show me 2025” matches neither condition. The app therefore treats it as having no period, clears whatever 2025 window the model emitted, and inherits the prior answer's window instead. This directly violates the requirement that a follow-up naming a year answer for that year regardless of the model or previous window.
findings.title: Not done: Named-year follow-ups can still inherit the previous period

findings.body: The new coverage invokes `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, which substitutes the provider, executor/database, audit, dimensions, and selection resolver with fakes. The frontend Ask tests also mock the API, while the repository test command contains no Playwright/browser suite and no Playwright specifications are present. Consequently the required user-facing flows—named-period follow-ups, no-period inheritance or aggregation, and period-control reruns—remain unproven through a browser, running API, and real database.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
